title: Single-Case Designs and N-of-1 Trials in Your Own Clinic

hook.en: Large trials tell you what works on average. But your patient is one person. An N-of-1 trial lets you test, on that one person, whether a treatment really helps them, using nothing more than a notebook and a plan.
hook.ur: Bade trials batate hain ke average mein kya kaam karta hai. Lekin aap ka mareez ek insaan hai. N-of-1 trial aap ko is ek insaan par aazmane deta hai ke ilaaj sach mein unhein faida deta hai ya nahi, sirf ek copy aur ek plan ke saath.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what a single-case or N-of-1 design is, plan a simple A-B-A-B test for one patient, know which conditions suit it and which do not, and read the results honestly.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke single-case ya N-of-1 design kya hai, ek mareez ke liye saada A-B-A-B test plan karenge, jaanenge kin halaton mein munasib hai aur kin mein nahi, aur nateeje imaandari se parhenge.

text.en: In a **single-case experimental design**, one person acts as their own control. You measure an outcome repeatedly across phases: baseline (A), treatment (B), withdrawal (A) and treatment again (B). If the outcome improves in each B phase and falls back in each A phase, the treatment is a likely cause. An **N-of-1 trial** adds randomisation of the order and, often, blinding. These designs work best for **stable, chronic, symptom-based problems** where the effect starts and stops quickly.
text.ur: **Single-case experimental design** mein ek shakhs apna control khud hota hai. Aap nateeja baar baar mukhtalif marahil mein naapte hain: baseline (A), ilaaj (B), wapsi (A) aur dobara ilaaj (B). Agar har B marhale mein nateeja behtar ho aur har A marhale mein wapas gir jaye to ilaaj ke wajah hone ka imkaan hai. **N-of-1 trial** tarteeb ki randomisation aur aksar blinding bhi jorta hai. Yeh designs **mustaqil, dair-pa, alamat par mabni masail** ke liye behtar hain jahan asar jaldi shuru aur band ho.

text.en: Think of **testing a new pair of shoes**. You wear the old pair for a week, the new pair for a week, the old again, then the new again, and note your foot pain each day. If pain drops every time you wear the new pair, you can trust it more than a one-time guess. The patient is the experiment.
text.ur: **Naye jootay aazmana** sochein. Ek haftay purane, ek haftay naye, phir purane, phir naye pehente hain aur har din paon ka dard likhte hain. Agar har baar naye jootay mein dard kam ho to ek baar ke andaaze se zyada bharosa kar sakte hain. Mareez khud tajurba hai.

steps.title: Choose one outcome and a daily measure
steps.detail: For example, pain at its worst each day (0 to 10) or minutes walked. Keep it simple enough to record every day. || Ek outcome aur rozana naap chunein

steps.title: Collect a baseline (A1)
steps.detail: Record for at least 5 to 7 days with no change in care, so you can see how stable the problem is. || Baseline (A1) jama karein

steps.title: Alternate the treatment on and off
steps.detail: Run phases of equal length (for example one week each): treatment on (B1), off (A2), on (B2). Change only one thing at a time. || Ilaaj ko on aur off karein

steps.title: Plot and look
steps.detail: Draw the daily scores on a simple chart and see whether the line moves each time the treatment starts and stops. Share the chart with the patient. || Chart bana kar dekhein

question.en: Which problem is best suited to an N-of-1 or A-B-A-B test?
question.ur: Kaun sa masla N-of-1 ya A-B-A-B test ke liye behtareen hai?

text.en: Stable chronic headache where a new neck routine could be started and stopped weekly
text.ur: Mustaqil chronic sar dard jahan gardan ki nayi routine hafta ba hafta shuru aur band ki ja sake

feedback.en: Yes — a stable, symptom-based problem with quick on and off effects fits.
feedback.ur: Haan — mustaqil, alamat par mabni masla jis mein asar jaldi on aur off ho, munasib hai.

feedback.en: Treatment cannot be stopped and started.
feedback.ur: Ilaaj ko rok kar dobara shuru nahi kiya ja sakta.

text.en: An acute ankle sprain that will heal in two weeks anyway
text.ur: Acute takhne ki moch jo do haftay mein waise bhi theek ho jayegi

feedback.en: The condition changes by itself, so phases cannot be compared.
feedback.ur: Halat khud badalti hai, isliye marahil ka muqabla nahi ho sakta.

question.en: In an A-B-A-B test the pain drops during B1, stays low in A2 when treatment is stopped, and drops a bit more in B2. What is the best reading?
question.ur: A-B-A-B test mein B1 mein dard girta hai, A2 mein jab ilaaj roka jata hai tab bhi kam rehta hai, aur B2 mein thora aur girta hai. Behtareen tabsira kya hai?

text.en: Clear proof that the treatment works
text.ur: Saaf saboot ke ilaaj kaam karta hai

feedback.en: The pain did not return when treatment stopped.
feedback.ur: Ilaaj band hone par dard wapas nahi aaya.

text.en: Proof that the treatment is harmful
The pattern does not show a treatment effect; the improvement may be natural recovery or a lasting effect, so you cannot tell
text.ur: Pattern ilaaj ka asar nahi dikhata; behtari qudrati recovery ya lambay asar ki ho sakti hai, isliye farq nahi bata sakte

feedback.en: Yes — a clear effect should move with the treatment, not just continue downward.
feedback.ur: Haan — saaf asar ilaaj ke saath hilna chahiye, sirf neeche jari nahi rehna.

question.en: Why do N-of-1 results not apply to everyone?
question.ur: N-of-1 nateeje har kisi par kyun lagu nahi hote?

text.en: They test one person under their own conditions, so they inform that patient's care, not general practice
text.ur: Yeh ek shakhs ko uske apne halaat mein aazmate hain, isliye us mareez ki care ko batate hain, aam practice ko nahi

feedback.en: Yes — their strength is personal, not general.
feedback.ur: Haan — in ki taqat zaati hai, aam nahi.

text.en: They are always biased against treatment
text.ur: Yeh hamesha ilaaj ke khilaaf biased hote hain

text.en: They are too short for any use
text.ur: Yeh kisi bhi istemal ke liye bohat mukhtasar hain

feedback.en: They can be useful for one patient's decision.
feedback.ur: Yeh ek mareez ke faisle ke liye mufeed ho sakte hain.

text.en: **Using it where the condition changes or the effect lingers.** Acute injuries improve on their own, and treatments with long carry-over, such as strengthening, do not switch off in a week. If the effect lingers, phases blur together. Also do not forget a long enough baseline, equal phase lengths and a plan agreed with the patient beforehand.
text.ur: **Aise masle mein istemal karna jahan halat badalti ho ya asar tikta ho.** Acute chotein khud theek hoti hain, aur lambay carry-over wale ilaaj, jaise strengthening, ek haftay mein band nahi hote. Agar asar tika rahe to marahil ghul mil jate hain. Kaafi lamba baseline, barabar marahil aur pehle se mareez ke saath tay shuda plan na bhoolein.

text.en: **Make the patient the co-scientist.** For example: "Let us test this properly. For one week we keep things as they are and you rate your pain each evening. Then we start the exercise for a week, stop for a week and start again. The chart will tell us both whether it helps you." Patients often adhere better when they see their own data.
text.ur: **Mareez ko saathi scientist banayein.** Misaal: "Aaiye iska theek se test karte hain. Ek haftay sab waise hi rahe aur aap har shaam dard rate karein. Phir ek haftay exercise, ek haftay band, aur dobara shuru. Chart hum dono ko batayega ke aap ko faida hai ya nahi." Mareez apna data dekh kar aksar behtar amal karte hain.

question.en: If one person's data are so limited, why do journals publish single-case studies?
question.ur: Agar ek shakhs ka data itna mehdood hai to journals single-case studies kyun shaya karte hain?

answer.en: A well-designed single-case study with repeated phases and a clear pattern can be as convincing as a group study for that person, and many replications across people build general knowledge. In rehabilitation, where patients vary widely, it is a practical way to find what works for whom.
answer.ur: Achhe design wali single-case study jis mein baar baar marahil aur saaf pattern ho us shakhs ke liye group study jitni qaail kar sakti hai, aur kai logon mein dohrane se aam ilm banta hai. Rehabilitation mein jahan mareez bohat mukhtalif hote hain, yeh dhoondhne ka amali tareeqa hai ke kis ke liye kya kaam karta hai.

beats.patient: A 55-year-old man has chronic knee pain and wonders whether a knee brace helps. His pain is steady at about 5 out of 10 each day.
beats.assessment: A stable, chronic, symptom-based problem where a brace can be put on and off, so an A-B-A-B plan fits.
beats.treatment: One week baseline, then a week with the brace, a week without, and a week with, rating pain every evening and noting the weather and walking.
beats.reassess: The chart shows his pain falls to 3 in both brace weeks and rises to 5 in the off week, so the brace is likely to help him; he buys one confidently.

text.en: **Never withhold needed care for a test.** If the condition could worsen without treatment, such as post-surgical rehabilitation or neurological decline, do not run an off phase. Agree stopping rules with the patient: if pain rises above an agreed level or red flags appear, the test stops and normal care resumes.
text.ur: **Test ke liye zaroori care na rokein.** Agar ilaaj ke baghair halat bigad sakti ho, jaise surgery ke baad rehab ya neurological girawat, to off phase na chalayein. Mareez ke saath rokne ke qaide tay karein: agar dard tay shuda satah se oopar jaye ya red flags aayen to test ruk jata hai aur aam care shuru ho jati hai.

text.en: Guyatt and colleagues reported three years of N-of-1 randomised trials in clinical practice, finding that they could change management and help patients and physicians reach clear decisions in a large share of cases. The CENT 2015 statement, an extension of CONSORT, provides a checklist for reporting N-of-1 trials, including how treatment periods were randomised, how outcomes were measured and how carry-over was handled.
text.ur: Guyatt aur saathiyon ne clinical practice mein teen saal ke N-of-1 randomised trials ki report di, jis mein paya gaya ke woh care badal sakte hain aur mareezon aur doctoron ko cases ke bade hisse mein saaf faisle tak pohanchne mein madad de sakte hain. CENT 2015 statement, jo CONSORT ki extension hai, N-of-1 trials ki report ke liye checklist deta hai, jis mein shamil hai ke ilaaj ke marahil kaise randomise hue, outcomes kaise naape gaye aur carry-over kaise sambhala gaya.

text.en: **One outcome, Baseline, Switch, Chart.** Pick one outcome, record a baseline, switch the treatment on and off, and chart the results.
text.ur: **Ek outcome, Baseline, Badlein, Chart.** Ek outcome chunein, baseline likhein, ilaaj on aur off karein, aur nateeje chart karein.

summary.en: A single-case or N-of-1 design uses one person as their own control across baseline and treatment phases.
summary.ur: Single-case ya N-of-1 design ek shakhs ko baseline aur ilaaj ke marahil mein apna control banata hai.

summary.en: It suits stable, chronic, symptom-based problems with quick on and off effects, not acute or lingering ones.
summary.ur: Yeh mustaqil, chronic, alamat par mabni masail ke liye hai jahan asar jaldi on off ho, acute ya tikne wale ke liye nahi.

summary.en: Results guide that patient's care, never withhold needed treatment, and set stopping rules.
summary.ur: Nateeje us mareez ki care ko batate hain, zaroori ilaaj na rokein, aur rokne ke qaide tay karein.

front.ur: Kin halaton ke liye N-of-1 test munasib hai?

back.en: Stable, chronic, symptom-based problems with quick effects.
back.ur: Mustaqil, chronic, alamat par mabni masail jin mein asar jaldi ho.

back.en: An effect that lingers after the treatment stops.
back.ur: Woh asar jo ilaaj band hone ke baad bhi rehta hai.

front.en: Does N-of-1 evidence apply to everyone?
front.ur: Kya N-of-1 evidence har kisi par lagu hota hai?

back.en: No; it informs that patient's own care.
back.ur: Nahi; yeh us mareez ki apni care ko batata hai.

note.en: Why one before-and-after story is not enough.
note.ur: Ek before-and-after kahani kyun kaafi nahi.
